note: Campground and Old Western Saloon about 6 mi south of Red Wing in the Hay Creek valley, bordering the Richard J. Dorer Memorial Hardwood State Forest; a separate horse camp has trail access. Most of the campground is permanent (seasonal) sites; the creekside rows are among them. --Claude
summary: Operator pages + 2026 map: $50 a day water/electric (tent $40, monthly $800, seasonal $2,100-2,500), 20/30/50 amp, dump, laundry, phone reservations. Price at the $50 line (not over); Google 4.5 (409). LONG-STAY: the 2026 map marks most sites 'Permanent camping' - five tests reported; reviewer reports seasonals favoured. Not waterfront kept; phone added in flags.
flags: LONG-STAY / MOSTLY SEASONAL (reviewer decides): the operator's 2026 campground map colours roughly 110+ sites green 'PERMANENT CAMPING' (1-14, 17-77, 83-91, 96, BB-GG, Q-Z, AA, several H sites), about 10 blue 'MONTHLY CAMPING' (92-102), yellow horse sites, red tent sites (15, 16, 78-80, C1-C2, H1-H3), and about 24 sites in WHITE with no legend entry (105-112 and A-P), which appear to be the transient sites. Five tests: (1) mostly seasonal - YES on the map; (2) nightly price posted - YES, '$50 Water & Electricity' daily rate on the operator's own page; (3) occupancy - no booking engine, phone only, could not check; (4) nightly share - about 24 of ~180 (~13%) if the white sites are the nightly ones, above 1 in 10 but the legend does not say so; (5) no homes or lots for sale. Newest Google reviews: 2/5 (edited 2 months ago) 'Terrible service if your not a seasonal they will treat you like an outcast'; 1/5 Tripadvisor (3 months ago) 'its going to be loud as a frat party all night'; 5/5 (4 weeks ago) 'Drive-thru RV sites ... Priced very fairly'; 5/5 (3 months ago) 'Great camping location'. Google 4.5 from 409, RV Life 4.5 (stored), so the under-4-stars auto-drop does not apply. I read it as mostly seasonal but with a posted nightly rate and a block of transient sites: borderline, not a clear drop.

PRIVATE GATE: $50 a day (water & electric), exactly at the US$50 line, not over it; the rate page says nothing about tax or mandatory per-night fees. No gateway within 40 km (St. Paul 67 km). Family has not stayed here. Presence: operator website with phone and a dated 2026 map; Google Maps 4.5 from 409 reviews.
Phone: none stored. Every operator page: 'Office/Restaurant: ... 651-359-8457' (also Google Maps). apply.py does not write phones: add 651-359-8457.

Waterfront: not waterfront kept. On the operator map Hay Creek (a trout stream) runs beside sites 54-61, 40-43, 36-39.4 and 7H-8H, but those are green 'Permanent camping' sites, plus tent sites 78-80 and C1-C2; none of the white (apparently nightly) sites is near the creek. No upgrade lead for bookable RV sites.
OHV: rules say 'No side by sides, four wheelers, dirt bikes'; a reviewer mentions a 'utvs run that day' (an event). General campground, not an OHV base; no flag beyond noting it.

Sites: stored count 175 and pull_through true (derived from old note prose) are not stated on any operator page; left alone. A reviewer: 'Drive-thru RV sites'. Season: not stated on the operator's pages; none stored.
Website OK: https://haycreekcampground.com/ (live, phone on every page). The /about/ and /contact/ menu links return 'This page doesn't seem to exist'. Pin OK (Google 44.48973,-92.54773, ~25 m).
